question_text: Determine the specific strength of the strongest $\mathrm{Al}, \mathrm{Mg}, \mathrm{Cu}, \mathrm{Ti}$, and Ni alloys. Use the densities of the pure metals, in $\mathrm{lb} / \mathrm{in} .^3$, in your calculations. Give your answer as a tuple: (specific_strength_Al, specific_strength_Cu, specific_strength_Ni).The units of each required answer are (in, in, in), respectively.
response:
The specific strength is the alloy strength divided by the pure-metal density:

- **Al (7075-T6):** \(73{,}000\ \text{psi}/0.0975\ \text{lb/in}^3 \approx 7.49\times10^5\ \text{in}\)
- **Cu (beryllium copper):** \(172{,}000\ \text{psi}/0.324\ \text{lb/in}^3 \approx 5.31\times10^5\ \text{in}\)
- **Ni (strongest Ni alloy):** \(106{,}000\ \text{psi}/0.322\ \text{lb/in}^3 \approx 3.29\times10^5\ \text{in}\)

Rounded to the precision expected:

\[
\boxed{(750000.0,\ 530000.0,\ 330000.0)}
\]
